question: Which of the following disorders is associated with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia ?:

options.opd: Crigler-Najjar syndrome Types I and II.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> increased levels of indirect bilirubin -> Dubin-Johnson syndrome -> 90% CHAIN: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> elevated levels of unconjugated bilirubin -> Rotor syndrome -> 85% CHAIN: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> impaired bilirubin conjugation -> Crigler-Najjar syndrome Types I and II -> 90% CHAIN: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> reduced hepatic uptake of bilirubin -> Intrahepatic cholestasis -> 90%
analysis: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia is primarily associated with disorders that impair the uptake, conjugation, or excretion of bilirubin by the liver. Among the options provided, Dubin-Johnson syndrome and Crigler-Najjar syndrome Types I and II are known to be associated with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
